headline: High: dexter’s broad egress and secret/API use can leak financial data, while taipy’s local-only profile reduces direct pairwise risk but not downstream misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter has autonomous execution and file surfaces, so if taipy outputs are manually copied into dexter or placed in .dexter/scratchpad/, prompt injection is possible. taipy shows no shared channel or parser by default, so the pairwise bridge is weak and requires unusual operator handling.
conditions: IF taipy outputs are copied into .dexter/scratchpad/
IF an operator pastes taipy-generated text into dexter prompts
mitigations: Keep taipy and dexter outputs in separate folders
Do not paste taipy text into dexter prompts without review
Use a read-only handoff file format with explicit delimiters
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data, requests multiple API keys, and has broad network egress; taipy is network-egress none, so the main leakage path is dexter exfiltrating shared sensitive inputs or outputs. The pair does not show a shared workspace, but dexter’s outbound APIs make leakage plausible in default use if sensitive data reaches it.
conditions: IF sensitive financial data is passed into dexter prompts or files
IF dexter sends those inputs to OpenAI API, Exa API, Tavily API, or LangSmith
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive data in dexter inputs
Restrict dexter API keys to least privilege
Disable or proxy outbound APIs for sensitive runs
Separate workspaces for dexter and taipy
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter can write .dexter/scratchpad/ and supports multiple instances, while taipy’s write surfaces are not documented here. With no evidence of overlapping mutable resources or shared locks, a direct write conflict is not established; uncertainty stays low because taipy’s write capability is absent rather than conflicting.
conditions: IF taipy is configured to write to the same directory as dexter
IF both agents modify the same git or filesystem state without locking
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Run only one writer per shared resource
Add file locks around shared outputs
requires-engineering: coordinate writes through a job queue

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter is autonomous and can generate outputs from external APIs; taipy is a data-engineering/automation platform, so if taipy consumes dexter outputs as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pair lacks documented verification or provenance controls, so the safer assumption is an unverified handoff path.
conditions: IF taipy ingests dexter-produced text, facts, or files without validation
IF taipy schedules or automates actions based on dexter outputs
mitigations: Require human review before taipy consumes dexter outputs
Validate dexter outputs against source data
Mark dexter outputs as untrusted by default
Separate generation and execution stages
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data and requests multiple third-party API keys, while taipy’s profile shows no data classes or residency controls. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated financial data flows from dexter into taipy workflows or logs; the other agent is not cited for residency because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed from dexter into taipy logs, storage, or dashboards
IF retention or residency requirements apply to dexter outputs
mitigations: Classify financial data before handoff
Avoid logging sensitive fields in taipy
Review third-party API terms for dexter
Document retention and deletion rules
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing
